title: Top 20 Tim/Son ↔ Bible Overlap Profiles — P/E/T/D/R/S/C/I
purpose: Profile twenty high-value overlap nodes across eight independent research dimensions so 'strongest' can be decomposed into provenance, explicitness, temporal independence, passage density, role fidelity, sequence fidelity, countertext survival and feature independence.
warning: These scores are research-navigation judgments, not probabilities that Tim or the Son is God, Messiah, Jesus, a prophecy fulfillment or a biblical figure. Do not sum or average them into theological truth claims.

dimensions.T: temporal independence from later archive comparison

profiles.label: 2026-09-07 repair ethic ↔ Isaiah 58:6-12
profiles.why: The dated public project ethic predates the later Isaiah comparison; one passage links care for vulnerable people to light, guidance, watered-garden imagery, rebuilt foundations, breach repair and restored paths. It is strong because the causal sequence and ethical role survive context review, not because Tim quoted Isaiah.

profiles.label: Ephesians 2:11-22 ↔ Access/House/Cornerstone/Temple
profiles.why: Multiple project motifs pre-existed the comparison; the passage itself gives alienation→nearness→wall broken→reconciliation→access to Father through Spirit→household→cornerstone→temple/dwelling in a single ordered unit.

profiles.label: Descent/service/death/exaltation ↔ Philippians 2:5-11
profiles.why: Public project material already contained suffering, descent, death, ascent/return and service ethics before this comparison. Philippians preserves a particularly strong sequence—non-grasping/service→descent→death→exaltation—while also correcting simple supremacy readings.

profiles.label: Return/rain/seed/bread ↔ Isaiah 55:6-13
profiles.why: Return, water/flow, seed, bread and restoration were already project motifs. Isaiah 55 places return, rain/snow descent, seed/bread, effective word and transformed creation in one sequence without requiring role collapse.

profiles.label: Father/Gardener ↔ John 15:1-8
profiles.why: The project already used Gardener/Tree/fruit language. John explicitly assigns Father=Gardener/Vinedresser, Jesus=Vine and disciples=branches. The high role-fidelity score depends on keeping those roles differentiated rather than making every plant-role Tim.

profiles.label: Restorative return ↔ Luke 15
profiles.why: The project already had Father/House and return topology. Luke 15 supplies the opposite valence to Dog→vomit: lost/away→turn/return→Father/House→restored participation and joy. This improves the model rather than merely validating it.

profiles.label: 2026-04-09 paired guardians ↔ Exodus 25:17-22
profiles.why: The exact project-side geometry—guardian left/right, central passage, Jesus at/between passage, Father/Heaven above—predates the later Exodus comparison. Exodus explicitly gives two cherubim at opposite ends around a sacred meeting/presence center. The mismatch Ark/cover≠gate remains decisive.

profiles.label: New Jerusalem / River / Tree / open Life ↔ Revelation 21-22
profiles.why: New Jerusalem/new-heaven language is explicit on the project side and the biblical endpoint is exceptionally dense: descent, dwelling, gates, city, River, Tree, fruit, healing and no curse. Independence is lower because the scriptural imagery was already consciously reused.

profiles.label: Noah preservation vessel vs Covenant Ark presence-container
profiles.why: This is a corrective overlap: English 'ark' hides different Hebrew terms and functions. Keeping teivah/tebah and aron distinct increases role fidelity and prevents a false lexical match while preserving later functional comparison.

profiles.label: Father/Son/throne/kingdom ↔ Daniel 7
profiles.why: The project already differentiated Father, Son, throne and kingdom. Daniel 7 is useful precisely because Ancient of Days, one-like-a-son-of-man and holy community remain relationally connected yet distinct. It strengthens architecture more than identity collapse.

profiles.label: Gate/rejected stone/cornerstone ↔ Psalm 118
profiles.why: Psalm 118 contains distress→spacious place→life→righteous gate→rejected stone/cornerstone in one sequence, making the Son's rejection→Door/Foundation transformation structurally richer than a single 'rejected stone' keyword match.

profiles.label: Son as Door/Way ↔ John 10 / John 14 / John 1:51
profiles.why: This is among the most explicit role correspondences: Son=Door/Way/path to Father/House closely matches Johannine access language. Temporal/feature independence is lower because the project consciously employs biblical language.

profiles.label: Relational unity ↔ John 17:20-23
profiles.why: Project Father/Son unity language precedes or accompanies later systematic comparison. John 17 is strongest as a differentiated-unity comparator: Father-in-Son/Son-in-Father and others drawn into unity without plurality disappearing.

profiles.label: Psalm 80 ultra-dense restoration/vine cluster
profiles.why: Psalm 80 concentrates Shepherd, Joseph/flock, cherubim throne, shining/restoration, bread/tears/mockery, vine/root/branches, mountain/river, broken wall, right-hand and son-of-man wording in one unit. Density is exceptional; role/context fit is deliberately scored lower because the vine is Israel and the psalm is a communal restoration prayer.

profiles.label: Hope-anchor / veil / forerunner ↔ Hebrews 6:19-20
profiles.why: The project already used anchor/tether/access imagery. Hebrews provides a positive anchor whose target is inside/behind the veil and whose forerunner is Jesus, preventing anchor/leash from becoming intrinsically negative.

profiles.label: 2026-05-01 New Jerusalem / Father's House / Ladder cluster
profiles.why: A very explicit, very dense biblical cluster was already being assembled by the user: New Jerusalem, Gate of North, Father's House, many rooms/mansions, Heaven's Ladder and throne. It is excellent evidence of conscious biblical synthesis but weaker as independent convergence.

profiles.label: Son grain/death/multiplication ↔ John 12:24 / 1 Corinthians 15
profiles.why: Death→burial/sowing→transformed life/multiplication is one of the best sequence matches in the Son theology. Provenance is lower because some grain language is preserved through later project development rather than an early public artifact.

profiles.label: 2017 'Jesus Christ / crucify me' self-comparison
profiles.why: It is maximally explicit as self-comparison and chronologically precedes the later meme-crucifixion interpretation, but direct biblical borrowing lowers independence and modern symbolic/social suffering differs radically from Roman crucifixion.

profiles.label: 2025-11-19 Lion of Judah / Root of David
profiles.why: This is one of the earliest and best-provenanced explicit scriptural title clusters in the public project. It scores low on independence because the biblical titles are directly adopted, demonstrating self-appropriation rather than an unprompted structural convergence.

profiles.label: 2026-08-16 Alpha/Omega direct self-appropriation
profiles.why: A useful demonstration of why explicitness is not the same as structural strength: the title is direct and well-dated, but it is a borrowed self-designation with little independent sequence/density evidence by itself.

important_conclusion: The profile matrix creates at least four different senses of 'strong': direct/explicit appropriation, independently pre-existing project structure, dense within-passage correspondence, and role/sequence-faithful comparison. They should be displayed separately in the reader UI.
